summary: Latency regression on L4 after runtime 1.19 upgrade for Qwen-family (long-context prompts)
description:
Customer report (via Support): After upgrading Dedicated cluster to runtime 1.19.x, AcmeAI is seeing a latency regression on NVIDIA L4 nodes for Qwen-family models. Regression is most pronounced for long-context prompts (4k–8k prompt tokens) and mixed prefill/decode workloads.

Issue summary
- What changed: runtime upgrade to 1.19.x (customer notes this coincided with "kernel selector changes" mentioned in release notes).
- What broke: p95 latency and overall throughput degraded on L4 only; A100 nodes in same environment appear unchanged.
- Scope: Qwen-family model; other models in their fleet reportedly unaffected.

Impact
- Customer-facing: noticeable latency increase in production traffic (chat completions) on L4-backed capacity.
- Reported metrics (customer):
  - Before (runtime 1.18.x): p95 end-to-end ~320–380ms for their common workload; prefill-heavy requests ~650–800ms.
  - After (runtime 1.19.x): p95 end-to-end ~520–650ms; prefill-heavy requests ~1.1–1.4s.
  - Tokens/sec decreased ~15–25% on L4.

Environment
- Deployment: Redwood Dedicated
- Region: us-east
- GPU: NVIDIA L4 (primary), comparison A100 pool
- Runtime: 1.19.0 -> 1.19.1 (customer tested both)
- Traffic profile: long prompts + streaming responses; mixture of 1–4 concurrent requests per instance; context length often 6k–10k.

Steps to reproduce (customer)
1) Route traffic to L4 pool (same model + same prompt set used before upgrade).
2) Use prompts with >= 4k tokens (their production distribution includes 6k–10k frequently).
3) Observe p95 latency increase vs pre-upgrade baselines.

Request samples / identifiers (customer)
- Example request IDs:
  - req_01HTY9N9K5Q9J3E6S2KJ3A8V1M
  - req_01HTY9P1Q0MZ7R8WZ0R4G8QW7T
- Time window with spikes: 2026-02-03 16:00–19:30 UTC

Customer-provided logs (excerpt)
- "x-redwood-runtime-version: 1.19.1"
- "x-redwood-gpu-sku: L4"
- "x-redwood-model: qwen2.5-7b-instruct"
- Streaming start delay increased; overall completion time increased.

Initial hypothesis (Support triage)
- Likely kernel selection regression specific to L4 + long-context prefill regime for Qwen-family.
- Candidate cause: selector v2 choosing a kernel optimized for A100/H100 that performs worse on L4 under long-context, or seq-bucket boundary misclassification causing wrong prefill kernel on L4.

Internal links
- Related internal Slack investigation thread: sources/slack/eng-runtime/thread_1737398821_900114.json
comments: 2026-02-03 17:12 UTC — Kira Thompson (Support): Created ticket from AcmeAI report. Asking Runtime to confirm whether kernel selector v2 is enabled by default in 1.19 for Dedicated and whether L4 has known regressions for long-context prompts. Linked request IDs and time window above.

2026-02-03 20:05 UTC — Connor O'Brien (Release Eng): +1 to immediate mitigation. If we disable v2 for that customer pool, we should confirm rollback success via selector_version breakdown + latency p95 over 30–60 minutes. Please document final override config in ticket for auditability.

2026-02-04 09:12 UTC — Kira Thompson (Support): Customer confirms latency returned to normal after override/rollback. They request an ETA for re-enabling v2, as they want benefits on other models but can’t accept regression on Qwen workload.

2026-02-06 16:37 UTC — Yuki Sato (GPU SKU Behavior): Reproduced in benchmark-lab on L4 with Qwen-family long-context prompts (6k–10k). The v2-selected L4 kernel is ~18–22% slower in prefill than v1 path. Believed root cause: incorrect seq-bucket boundary + missing tuned L4 entry for Qwen-family long-context.

2026-02-07 11:08 UTC — Grace Kim (Kernel Selection): Fixes in flight: (1) update registry entries for Qwen-family on L4 (new kernel id for long-context prefill) and (2) seq bucket boundary bugfix. Tracking in PRs: sources/github/redwood/pr_18533_add_registry_entry_for_qwen_family.json and sources/github/redwood/pr_18571_fix_seq_bucket_off_by_one.json.

2026-02-09 18:55 UTC — Omar El-Sayed (Runtime Integration): Fix validated on staging L4 and in perf sweep for the customer’s prompt set approximation. Plan: re-enable selector v2 for AcmeAI at 5% on L4 pool during low-traffic window, with rollback if p95 regresses >8% vs baseline for 30 min.

2026-02-10 03:20 UTC — Aisha Bello (SRE): Canary re-enable completed (5% then 25%). No p95 regression observed; kernel_choice now shows updated L4 entry for Qwen-family long-context. Error rates normal. OK to restore default config for this pool.

2026-02-10 05:02 UTC — Kira Thompson (Support): Notified AcmeAI that selector v2 has been re-enabled with updated L4 tuning; asked them to confirm from their side. Provided rollback instructions and offered to keep a per-model-family pin if they want added safety during evaluation.
resolution: Mitigated immediately by disabling kernel selector v2 on AcmeAI’s L4 pool (restored baseline latency). Root cause identified as suboptimal/missing Qwen-family long-context L4 registry entry combined with seq-length bucket boundary misclassification. After registry + bucket-boundary fixes were validated, selector v2 was re-enabled via staged canary without regression. Ticket resolved after successful rollout and customer confirmation pending (no further issues reported during monitoring window).
